subject: BYO-Key ephemeral retention exception — pilot safeguards & next steps
messages:
From: Julie Morris <julie.morris@medcorehealth.com>
To: alex_martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 13:12:00 -0500
Subject: Short-term retention for BYO-key pilot (audit needs)

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the demo last week — our engineering team is ready to run a 6-week pilot using Redwood Private with BYO-Key for a small set of test tenants. Two quick asks from our DPO/security side before we proceed: 

1) For the pilot only, can Redwood retain ephemeral key usage logs (key creation/usage/rotation events) for 7 days instead of the standard 24 hours? We need that window to correlate with our incident monitoring.
2) We need a streaming feed (or scheduled export) of audit events related to BYO-key ops to our secure S3 bucket every 24 hours.

I attached our DPO requirements doc (MedCore-DPO-reqs.pdf) with exact fields they want in the feed. This is a pilot, so a time-boxed exception is fine — we just need confirmation of the technical path and a short risk acceptance note from Redwood.

Can you loop in the relevant folks and let us know the earliest you can enable this for the pilot?

Best,
Julie
Julie Morris
VP Product, MedCore Health
--
Attachment: MedCore-DPO-reqs.pdf (PDF, 85 KB)

From: alex_martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Short-term retention for BYO-key pilot (audit needs)

Folks — forwarding Julie's ask from MedCore. Pilot request: 7-day ephemeral key usage log retention + daily export to customer's S3. Time-boxed to the 6-week pilot.

Quick context: this would be an exception to our default ephemeral retention (24h) and touches audit pipeline, KMS rotation metadata, and transfer to external buckets (customer-managed).

Questions I want answered before I confirm back to the customer:
- Can infra support a 7-day retention window for BYO ephemeral metadata without impacting latency or storage tiering?
- What are the minimal audit fields we can guarantee in the export by EOD? (Julie's attachment lists many fields)
- Approvals/process: what does security need to sign off for a pilot exception?

Proposal (initial): Priyom, can you scope a short-run implementation that:
  a) toggles ephemeral retention to 7 days for a specific tenant tag,
  b) emits a daily gzipped JSONL export of audit events to an S3 presigned URL,
  c) includes an HMAC signed manifest so MedCore can validate integrity.

Naomi/Grace — need product and risks (comms, billing impact, rollback plan).

I can respond to Julie with a timeline (48-72h) if we have alignment.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
--

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: alex_martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 09:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Short-term retention for BYO-key pilot (audit needs)

Alex / team — quick tech triage below.

Feasibility: doable for a pilot with scoped controls. Implementation notes:
- Retention: ephemeral key metadata is stored in our audit-index layer (hot TTL-backed index). We can add a tenant-scoped override to set TTL to 7 days for ephemeral_key_event records. Storage cost estimate: ~2.5 GB/day for the pilot tenants (rough estimate from similar customers).
- Export: we already have an export connector that can stream audit JSONL to S3. We'll add a filter to only include BYO-key / key-rotation / key-usage events. Exports will be gzipped and HMAC-SHA256 signed per file.
- Integrity & scope: manifest will include start/end timestamps, record counts, and HMAC. We'll include event ids (uuid), timestamp, actor (service/user), object_id (key id), action, and rotation_metadata (old_key_id -> new_key_id references).

Constraints & risks:
- Log enrichment: some rotation details live only in KMS-agent debug logs for 12h; we must ensure rotation_metadata is written atomically into audit-index at rotation time, otherwise we may miss some correlations. I'll add a small hook in the KMS agent to emit rotation metadata synchronously for the pilot.
- Performance: enabling 7d TTL on a high-throughput tenant increases retention pressure on hot indices; recommend rate-limiting policy to keep pilot under agreed TPS.

Plan & timeline (if approved):
- 24h: small infra change to add tenant TTL override and export filter config (staged).
- 48h: enable on MedCore test tenant, produce first daily export to their S3.
- 72h: review sample exports with MedCore security, sign off.

I can run the infra changes and provide a short rollback (revert TTL override) in 30 minutes if we observe abnormal index pressure.

--
Priyom Das
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: alex_martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 13:08:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Short-term retention for BYO-key pilot (audit needs)

Thanks Priyom — this seems implementable as a pilot. A few product/risk items to capture before we commit: 

1) Time-boxed exception: pilot TTL change must be explicitly timeboxed in our config and automatically roll back at pilot end (we'll add an expiration tag).
2) Billing: storing 7 days of extra ephemeral logs will increase storage costs. We should bill as an "audit-export premium" line item for pilot customers or absorb initially under trial credits — ops to decide. Monica, can you propose billing treatment?
3) Security approval & runbook: Security needs a short acceptance note that documents why this exception is limited and how we'll validate integrity. Grace, can you own the runbook and acceptance checklist?
4) Customer comms: outbound to MedCore should make clear the pilot SLA (no SLA for durability beyond 7 days) and rollback behavior. Alex, please include rollback steps and contact for emergency reversion.

If we have alignment I approve the pilot posture. Priyom — please coordinate the infra changes and share sample exports to our internal secure drive for review.

Naomi Feldman
Director, Product — Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: alex_martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 10:45:00 -05:00
Subject: RE: Short-term retention for BYO-key pilot (audit needs)

Hi Julie — thanks for the clear ask and the DPO doc. Quick update and proposed next steps (pilot-only):

1) Scope: Redwood can enable a timeboxed 7-day retention of ephemeral key usage/rotation events for the MedCore pilot tenants. This will be enabled via a tenant TTL override that expires automatically at pilot end (we'll set expiration to 2028-02-25 unless you request otherwise).
2) Export: We will deliver a daily gzipped JSONL export of BYO-key audit events to the S3 bucket you provide. Each file will include a signed HMAC manifest and the minimal event fields our infra guarantees (uuid, ts, actor, object_id, action, rotation_metadata).
3) Timeline: target to have the export live and delivering a sample file within 48 hours of your approval. Full pilot enablement within 72 hours.
4) Risk & rollback: Priyom has added a synchronous rotation metadata hook to reduce missed correlations. If we see index pressure or errors, rollback (revert TTL override) can be done within 30 mins. We'll document the runbook and require MedCore to sign the pilot MOA.
5) Billing: Monica will follow up on billing treatment (temporary credit vs audit premium).

Next actions for MedCore: please confirm (a) acceptance of the expiration date (2028-02-25) or propose a different end date, and (b) provide a presigned S3 URL for ingest and the principal for cross-account write.

I'll attach an initial MOA draft and the audit schema for your review.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
